evidence: Parsed every task judge.toml with tomllib: gates/render 1 binary, gates/constraints 1 binary (both aggregation all_pass, scoring.toml:1-3 gates 0.0) - gates are binary-only as required. scored/functional 44 criteria, all binary (e.g. hro_job_open line 26, hro_restart); each is an observable pass/fail behaviour (refused/accepted, order equals X, status 401/403/409, appears within 15 s) with an explicit 'Fails if' clause - correct fit for binary. scored/polish 5 criteria, all binary (lines 20,29,38,47,56); despite the dimension name these are not craft: polish/prompt.md:14 says 'Judge how the workspace holds up while people work at the same time, not visual craft', and each row is an objectively checkable preservation outcome (draft text unchanged, document.activeElement unchanged, scroll offset not reset, explanation shown, sent once) tied to instruction.md:7 ('never touch my draft or my cursor', 'without losing my place'). Binary matches the template's polish dimension (template polish judge.toml: four binary criteria). scored/visual 5 criteria, all type='likert', points=5 (lines 20-21, 35-36, 50-51, 65-66, 80-81), each with a described anchor at every level 1..5 (regex confirms anchors {1,2,3,4,5} for hro_vis_type, hro_vis_color, hro_vis_layout, hro_vis_hierarchy, hro_vis_consistency), covering degree-of-quality craft (typography, palette/contrast, spacing/layout, hierarchy, component consistency). Anchor scale agrees with the pinned engine: Dockerfile:31 installs harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, whose Likert.prompt_fragment is 'an integer from 1 to {points}' and normalize is (raw-1)/(points-1) (models.py:44-50), so the 1..5 anchors map exactly onto the schema and raw 1 -> 0.0; visual/prompt.md:7,12,16 consistently prescribes 'Likert 1' (normalized zero) as the floor for gate failure/unobservable outcomes. This is actually tighter than the template's 0..5 anchors, which rely on a prompt override of the engine's 1..5 hint. The internal annotation ('Likert we dont use') is the documented known false positive (SKILL.md:65, quality-checks.md:170); the shipped template visual dimension itself uses likert, so likert here is correct. No binary criterion grades craft; no likert block lacks anchors; no gate holds likert. Attempted counterexamples: (a) broken app passing - a dead/static app cannot earn likert points because visual/prompt.md:11-12 gates every visual row to raw 1 (=0.0) on failure of a real backend check, and functional binaries all require a positive control; (b) conforming alternative failing - closest candidate is polish hro_pol_earlier_place (binary, 'same position on screen (within a few pixels)'), which is a near-continuous degree measure graded pass/fail; but the public ask is a discrete outcome ('pull in earlier ones without losing my place'), and 'a few pixels' is a tolerance on that outcome, not a craft gradation, so binary still fits. Its exact tolerance as a possible hidden precision belongs to the hidden-requirement/fairness rows, not to type fit. Runtime: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope states full configured grading is absent); row 41 is a static type/anchor-fit check fully decidable from source, so no measurement is required for this verdict. Whether likert anchors yield a useful score spread is owned by row 40, not claimed here.
